title: Quantization separation loop never separates a six-singularity cluster with curvatureBias = -1: 50 rounds, objective flat, VALIDITY VIOLATION
description:
With NDirectionField.curvatureBias set to -1 (the field is `public final double curvatureBias = 0` at NDirectionField.java:81, used in the Hodge-Laplacian assembly around lines 775-793), the cross field's singularities land close enough together that the quantization's CBK15 section 4 lazy separation loop never converges:

```
[quantize] separation round=46 mergedClusters=1 cuts=3
[quantize] state=OPTIMAL objective=147.363 zeroArcs=1194/1284 violations=0 round=47
[quantize] separation round=47 mergedClusters=1 cuts=4
[quantize] state=OPTIMAL objective=147.363 zeroArcs=1195/1284 violations=0 round=48
[quantize] separation round=48 mergedClusters=1 cuts=4
[quantize] state=OPTIMAL objective=147.363 zeroArcs=1194/1284 violations=0 round=49
[quantize] separation round=49 mergedClusters=1 cuts=4
[quantize] state=OPTIMAL objective=147.363 zeroArcs=1194/1284 violations=0 round=50
[quantize] VALIDITY VIOLATION merged singularity vertices=[375, 383, 385, 386, 2107, 2164]
[layout] clusters=9 singularClusters=7 skeletonArcs=90 tJunctions=1 featureEdgesOpen=0
[quad-layout] quantization 10.413s
```

Every round the ILP solves OPTIMAL at the same objective 147.363, ZeroArcCollapse finds the same cluster of six singularities merged through all-zero arcs, QuantizedMeshGrid.collectSeparationCuts adds 3-4 cuts (one BFS zero-arc path between two merged singularities, sum of quantized lengths >= 1), and the next solve satisfies those cuts by zeroing a different path through the same cluster. After MAX_SEPARATION_ROUNDS = 50 the loop gives up and marks singularitySeparationViolated; the layout then proceeds with a T-mesh that merges six singularities.

The cut is too weak: one path at a time cannot exhaust the zero paths through a six-singularity cluster, and the objective never moves because the ILP is never forced to pay for the separation. Candidates: a min-cut on the zero-arc graph between two merged singularities (every arc across the cut, not one path, sums to >= 1); all shortest zero paths of a cluster in one round; or the basis-loop formulation of PATCH-90, which is valid by construction. Whichever is chosen, the loop should also stop as soon as the objective and the cluster stop changing rather than spinning to the round cap.

This is distinct from PATCH-115 (fandisk: the ILP is infeasible because the T-mesh is broken upstream) and PATCH-69 (solver time). curvatureBias = 0 does not reproduce it; the bias is the trigger, the separation loop is the defect.

Mesh: bolt, ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_10/bolt_in_tri.off, loaded in QuadLayoutScene with curvatureBias set to -1 by hand. Bolt only loads end to end with PATCH-107's worktree diff (feature-alignment guard and carve end-crossing trim), so work this in a worktree synced after PATCH-107 lands.

Re-scoped 2026-09-19 after reading LCKB19 section 5.2 and LCK21a sections 4.1-4.2: neither paper repairs validity with lazy cuts. LCK21a guarantees validity a priori by Lemma 1, one constraint per trace over S_i* (Eq. 3), which QuantizedMeshGrid.addValidityConstraints already implements (the 'validity=40' in the log) and whose own metric expects SEPARATION_CUTS = 0. The lazy loop firing at all therefore means Lemma 1's premise is broken on bolt at bias -1: the traces' first-sector intersections are wrong, consistent with the 508 hop-law violations still logged at that bias after PATCH-114. The SingularitySeparationCuts block written in the first pass is a correct constraint but treats a symptom of broken tracing; it is dropped from the diff. The fix belongs in the motorcycle-graph construction so that Eq. 3 covers every singularity.

User direction 2026-09-19: curvatureBias = -1 is the goal for every mesh (it finds the high-curvature singularities people mean by cross-field singularities and gives cleaner parametrizations). Bias 0 is the legacy setting, not the target; the bias-0 regression checks in the definition of done are a sanity check, and the default should move to -1 once bolt, hand, rockerarm, buddha, fandisk, block and botijo all load at -1.
definition-of-done:
1. On bolt with curvatureBias = -1 the quantization ends with no '[quantize] VALIDITY VIOLATION' line, singularitySeparationViolated = false, and SEPARATION_CUTS = 0: the LCK21a Lemma 1 per-trace validity constraints (Eq. 3, QuantizedMeshGrid.addValidityConstraints) separate every singularity on their own, with no lazy cut round. The lazy separation loop stays as a safety net that the ticket shows never fires on bolt at bias 0, -0.25, -0.5 or -1, nor on hand, rockerarm, fandisk or buddha.
2. The ticket records, for the six merged singularities [375, 383, 385, 386, 2107, 2164], which of their traces had a wrong or missing first-sector intersection n_i* (validity fallback: noSectorMeeting / sectorMeetingWithoutNode, or a full-chain fallback), why (the tracing defect), and what the fix to the motorcycle-graph construction is. The fix is to the tracing, not to the quantization constraints.
3. Bolt at bias -1 logs zero motorcycle hop-law violations and zero Def 3.1 rectangularity violations, as it does at bias 0.
4. The curvature bias is the NDirectionField curvature_bias input port (default -1, no system property, no engine field, no scene key); the pipeline runs at -1 unless a node graph sets the port.
5. hand, rockerarm, bolt and buddha at bias 0 produce the same quantized arc lengths as master (same final '[quantize] state=OPTIMAL objective=... zeroArcs=...' line).
6. A unit test on a small hand-authored T-mesh shows a trace configuration where the Eq. 3 constraint was previously built on the wrong arc set and is now correct.
testing-plan:
1. Set NDirectionField.curvatureBias = -1 (it is a final field; make it a property or a ticket-scoped constant for the run), load the mesh in QuadLayoutScene and reproduce the log above; note the mesh name on the ticket.
2. Dump the zero-arc paths inside the merged cluster each round and confirm the cuts added in round N are satisfied in round N+1 by a different zero path.
3. Implement the stronger cut; rerun with bias -1 and with bias 0 on hand, rockerarm, bolt and buddha; compare objective and zeroArcs.
4. Screenshot of the quantized layout under tmp/ and a launch.json entry with the bias property.
changes-made: Reproduced with the cross-field curvature bias wired through the pipeline instead of a hand-edited final field: NDirectionField gained a curvature_bias input port (default 0), QuadLayoutEngine.curvatureBias hands it over, and QuadLayoutScene cycles it with K (0, -1, -0.5, -0.25) and logs '[quad-layout] curvature bias <v>'. No system property. NDirectionField.evaluate() had been discarding the configured node and solving on a fresh default instance, so the port had to be read there.
bolt at bias -1 reproduces the ticket exactly: arcs=1284, '[quantize] state=OPTIMAL objective=147.363 zeroArcs=1204/1284 violations=0 round=0', one merged cluster of six singularities.

Diagnosis: the old cut was one BFS zero path per round, and 'sum over that path >= 1' is satisfied by lengthening any single arc of it, so the next solve re-zeroes a parallel strand of the same corridor. Path packing did not help because the packed paths are arc-disjoint: a corridor whose strands share an arc (the common case) yields one path, and the solver pays on the non-shared half. Hence 50 rounds at a flat objective of 147.363 with the same six-singularity cluster.

Fix: SingularitySeparationCuts replaces the path cut with a cut condition the solver has to satisfy everywhere at once. Each merged cluster gets a block: its singularities are numbered in binary, every node of the corridor they merge through carries one 0/1 potential per code bit, the potentials are pinned to the code bits at the singularity nodes, and every arc inside the corridor carries |d(u) - d(v)| <= q(arc). A zero arc therefore forces its two ends to share every bit, so two singularities with different codes cannot stay joined by zero arcs at all - the solver picks the cut, instead of us naming one path. It cuts off no valid quantization: in any separated solution label each zero-arc component with the code of the one singularity it holds.

bolt, curvatureBias -1, after the change: separation converges in 11 rounds (12 solves) with 7 cut blocks, the last line being '[quantize] state=OPTIMAL objective=147.363 zeroArcs=1170/1284 violations=0 round=11' followed by '[layout] clusters=14 singularClusters=12 skeletonArcs=114 tJunctions=1 featureEdgesOpen=0'. No '[quantize] VALIDITY VIOLATION' line, singularitySeparationViolated=false. Before: 50 rounds, ~180 single-path cuts, objective flat at 147.363, '[quantize] VALIDITY VIOLATION merged singularity vertices=[375, 383, 385, 386, 2107, 2164]' and a layout with clusters=9 singularClusters=7. Quantization wall time 6.8-13.3s across runs against 10.4s for the old 50-round spin.

Loop stop: with the blocks keyed by merged-singularity set, a round that finds nothing new to block logs '[quantize] separation stalled round=N: every merged cluster's cut already spans its whole zero component, so the next solve repeats this one (objectiveMoved=.. clustersMoved=..)' and breaks instead of running to MAX_SEPARATION_ROUNDS. A block that is rerouted around is widened (its corridor is dilated by one more zero-arc hop each time) rather than duplicated, so the stall can only fire once a cut already covers its whole zero component.

Unknown 1 answered: smaller bias magnitudes do not trip the cluster. Sweeping bolt through the scene's K control gives bias 0: 22 singularities, objective=1536.279, zeroArcs=1005/1398, round=0; bias -0.25: 18 singularities, objective=1386.793, zeroArcs=977/1342, round=0; bias -0.5: 14 singularities, objective=1906.725, zeroArcs=751/1150, round=0 - none of them needs a single separation cut. Only bias -1 merges, and there the T-mesh itself has degenerated: arcs=1284 with classes=1125 (almost no side-pair merging), 1204 of 1284 arcs quantized zero, and the motorcycle stage reports 'hop turns: flat=810 ccwCorner=0 cwCorner=960 atSingularity=40 lawViolations=758' plus 'Def 3.1 rectangularity: violations=2 worstRelativeError=1.000000', against lawViolations=0 at every other bias. So this is the separation loop's weakness surfacing on a T-mesh that is already ill-formed, not the bias putting singularities on arcs the T-mesh cannot separate.

PATCH-114 connection: bolt at bias -1 shows the same upstream signature that ticket names. Its motorcycle stage logs 758 hop-law violations and Def 3.1 rectangularity violations=2 worstRelativeError=1.0, where every other bias has lawViolations=0; 40 hop turns land at singularities. That is consistent with separatrices being routed straight through cones instead of through ChartWalker.crossVertex, which is what PATCH-114 fixes in MotorcycleGraph.handleEdgeCrossing (this worktree still has the old corner-exit path: handleEdgeCrossing records edgeHit.cornerLocalIndex and calls walker.crossEdge, never crossVertex). The stronger cut therefore hardens the quantization against a T-mesh that PATCH-114 should stop producing; it is not a substitute for that fix. The cut is independent of it - it only ever adds constraints when a solve merges two singularities, so on a T-mesh PATCH-114 has cleaned up it costs nothing.

Out of scope, seen while verifying: bolt at bias -0.5 and -1 both fail after quantization, inside the layout-embedding carve before '[embed]' logs, with 'T-mesh nodes 165 and 166 both landed on copy vertex 3043; one mesh vertex never owns two T-mesh nodes'. Bias -0.5 needs no separation cut at all and fails the same way, so this is downstream of the quantization and independent of this ticket. It means the bias -1 layout cannot be rendered end to end, so there is no screenshot of it.

Unit test: ixdar-app/test/unit/mesh/SingularitySeparationCutTest.java over a new hand-authored fixture, ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/fixtures/singularity_cluster.dsl - three singularities (vertex ids 101, 102, 103) joined through one hub by three zero arcs, so the two zero paths share their first arc. With the shared arc weighted 5 and the branches 1, the single-path cut 'q(shared) + q(toB) >= 1' is satisfied by q(toB)=1 and ZeroArcCollapse still reports [[101, 103]] merged: a second round is needed. One cut block over the same cluster (three singularities, so two code bits) forces q(toB)=q(toC)=1 and leaves no merged cluster: one round. The fixture needed a 'vertex' input port on the network_node authoring node, since singularity identity is the source vertex id and the DSL had no way to set it.
Full unit suite after the change: Tests run: 294, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0.

curvatureBias 0 regression check, final quantize line before and after the change. bolt: 'OPTIMAL objective=1536.279 zeroArcs=1005/1398 violations=0 round=0' both, layout 'clusters=53 singularClusters=22 skeletonArcs=393 tJunctions=0' both. rockerarm: 'OPTIMAL objective=3252.913 zeroArcs=1545/2706 violations=0 round=0' both, layout identical. buddha: 'OPTIMAL objective=15347.516 zeroArcs=8053/17916 violations=0 round=0' both. Those three never enter the separation loop, so the new cut is never built for them. hand does: it took 38 separation rounds before and takes 2 now, same objective 3190.380, zeroArcs 2384 against 2385 and skeletonArcs 1352 against 1351 - one arc different among the many optima at that objective, with clusters=260 singularClusters=40 tJunctions=5 unchanged. Flagging that as the one number that moved: hand's old result was itself the end of 38 rounds of arbitrary single-path cuts, so which optimum it lands on was never stable.

Re-verified on top of PATCH-114 (master 2f5d8a65, synced with no conflict). The six-singularity cluster still forms at bias -1: routing corner exits through ChartWalker.crossVertex shrinks bolt's T-mesh from arcs=1284 to arcs=779 and cuts the motorcycle hop-law violations from 758 to 508, but the quantization's first solve still merges one cluster. No VALIDITY VIOLATION line, quantization 0.435s against the 10.413s of the old 50-round spin. So PATCH-114 reduces the problem but does not remove it, and the cut is what makes it terminate.

Post-PATCH-114, bolt at bias -0.5 newly merges too (it did not before: it used to finish at round 0 with arcs=1150 objective=1906.725). On 2f5d8a65 it is arcs=1056 objective=700.955, one merged cluster, separated in 7 rounds with 5 blocks, last line '[quantize] state=OPTIMAL objective=700.955 zeroArcs=871/1056 violations=0 round=7' then '[layout] clusters=19 singularClusters=14 skeletonArcs=185 tJunctions=1', no VALIDITY VIOLATION, 0.357s. So the cut is load-bearing at two bias settings now, not one.

Answering the cone question directly on 2f5d8a65: routing corner exits through crossVertex does change bolt's bias -1 T-mesh substantially - arcs 1284 to 779, classes 1125 to 653, Def 3.1 rectangularity violations 2 to 0, motorcycle hop-law violations 758 to 508 - so traces were indeed leaving faces at cones. It does not remove the merge: the first solve still puts six singularities in one zero cluster, and without a cut the loop still cannot separate them. PATCH-114 makes the corridor smaller, which is why the loop now needs 3 rounds instead of 11.

Full unit suite on the synced base (2f5d8a65): Tests run: 302, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, BUILD SUCCESS - including the new SingularitySeparationCutTest (PATCH-114 brought its own tests, which is why the count rose from 291).

Re-scoped at the user's direction: drop SingularitySeparationCuts, keep the bias wiring and the NDirectionField.evaluate() fix, and find why the Lemma 1 per-trace constraints fail to separate the cluster at bias -1.

Re-scope accepted. First diagnostic finding, and it supports the re-scope: at bias -1 the arrangement is not a T-mesh at all. On master 2f5d8a65, bolt logs '[motorcycle] arrangement patches: 289 cycles, 69 valid rectangles, 0 unresolved' at bias -1 against '679 cycles, 679 valid rectangles' at bias 0 - only 24 percent of the faces of the trace arrangement are rectangles. That is why the quantization looks degenerate downstream: classes=653 for arcs=779 (almost no opposite-side merging, against classes=102 for arcs=1398 at bias 0), consistency=12 against 62, and accumulatePerpendicularWeights gives zero objective weight to every arc bounded only by invalid cycles, which is where the tiny objective 147.363 and the 700 of 779 zero arcs come from.

Lemma 1's premise is not broken through the fallback paths: at bias -1 the log reads 'validity=40 (fallback=0) ... prefixFallbacks=0', so every one of the 40 traces found a first-sector meeting with a real intersection node and every S_i* prefix was found on the trace chain. The selection rule in addValidityConstraints (pick the recorded meeting with the smallest ourParametricLength among those with theirParametricLength < ourParametricLength) is the right reading of LCK21a: l_ji < l_ij is exactly 'the other singularity lies in the pi/2 sector around t_i'. So the constraints were built over 40 non-empty arc sets and still failed to separate. The suspect is therefore the set of recorded meetings itself - if a crossing is missing from trace.metOtherTraces, the minimum picked is a later intersection, S_i* is a superset of the true prefix, and the constraint is strictly weaker than Lemma 1 requires.

Mechanism found, and it is in the tracing. At bias -1 bolt has 256 nodes with an ambiguous port order ('[patch-diag] nodes with ambiguous port order: 256'), and the dumps show why: e.g. node 18 carries six ports of which two share the direction (0,-1) and two share (0,1) - one trace travelling -v passes through while another trace travelling +v passes through the same node along the same iso-line. Two traces overlap collinearly instead of one stopping. PatchBoundaryBuilder.sortPorts then has nothing to order them by, falls back to the arcId tie-break, and the arrangement walk fuses the surrounding faces: 220 of 289 cycles are invalid and the hop law fails 508 times, because arriving along one arc and leaving on the collinear partner is a 180 degree turn, neither flat nor a +-pi/2 corner.

Root cause in the code: FaceSegmentIndex.crossingsOf (the retroactive sweep that nodes crossings between concurrently traversed faces) skips same-axis pairs outright - 'existing.axis == fresh.axis' - and its own Javadoc admits 'it cannot see a collinear overlap'. earliestIntersection (the forward path) does see them, because intersectSegments has a same-axis branch that returns the first contact point of two chords on one iso-line, but MotorcycleGraph.handleIntersection then treats that contact as an ordinary crossing: it nodes it, records a meeting and calls advanceStateAlongLevel to carry the trace straight on along the other trace's track. A motorcycle that runs onto an existing track must crash there; instead both keep going and overlap. That is also why the trace's metOtherTraces is missing encounters, which is what breaks Lemma 1's premise: a collinear trace ahead has dv=0, so it is the innermost member of the pi/2 sector, and dropping it makes S_i* a superset of the true prefix.

Measured: bolt logs collinearMeetings=0 at bias 0 and collinearMeetings=193 at bias -1 (new counter on the '[motorcycle] done' line). That lines up one-to-one with the rest: 0 collinear meetings gives 679 of 679 valid rectangles, lawViolations=0 and no separation round; 193 gives 69 of 289 valid rectangles, 256 ambiguous port orders, lawViolations=508 and the lazy loop firing.

First tracing fix, in MotorcycleGraph.handleIntersection: a contact whose other segment runs on the same axis is a crash, not a crossing, so the trace is marked dead at the contact node instead of being carried on along the other trace's track (EGK*08 section 2 motorcycle rule; LCK21a section 3 keeps tracing through transversal crossings only). On bolt at bias -1 that moves every number the right way: collinearMeetings 193 to 4, nodes with ambiguous port order 256 to 8, valid rectangles 69 of 289 to 145 of 151, hop-law violations 508 to 12, and the quantization goes from objective=147.363 zeroArcs=1204/1284 to objective=1679.954 zeroArcs=206/342. Bias 0 is untouched (collinearMeetings=0 there, 679 of 679 rectangles as before). The lazy loop still fires, so this is not the whole defect.

Ruled out: the exact iso comparison in FaceSegmentIndex.intersectSegments ('if (isoA != isoB) return null') is not the problem. Instrumented it to count same-axis chord pairs whose spans overlap and whose iso values differ by less than 1e-6 - bolt reports nearCollinearSkips=0 at bias 0 and at bias -1, worst gap 0. Traces that share an iso-line share it bit-exactly, because both values come through the same chart arithmetic, so no tolerance is needed there.

Second tracing fix, in MotorcycleGraph.registerSegment: the retroactive sweep (contactsOf, which unlike crossingsOf does see collinear overlaps) noded a same-axis contact and recorded the meeting but left the trace alive, so a trace that ran onto an existing track while both were traversing the face concurrently kept going. Crashing there too takes bolt at bias -1 from 12 hop-law violations to 6 and from 145 of 151 rectangles to 151 of 154. A third gap: handleEdgeCrossing never re-checked trace.alive after registerSegment, so a trace crashed by the retroactive sweep carried on to the next face anyway; adding that check is what makes the crash actually stop it.

State after the two crash fixes, bolt at bias -1 against master: hop-law violations 508 to 6, valid rectangles 69 of 289 to 151 of 154, Def 3.1 rectangularity violations 0 (was 0 after PATCH-114 too), nodes with ambiguous port order 256 to 4, quantization objective 147.363 zeroArcs=1204/1284 to objective=1804.235 zeroArcs=193/337. The lazy loop now converges in 3 rounds with 3 single-path cuts and there is no VALIDITY VIOLATION line, where master spun 50 rounds and gave up. Bias 0 is bit-identical to master throughout (679 of 679 rectangles, lawViolations=0, objective=1536.279 zeroArcs=1005/1398 round=0). Not yet at the definition of done, which wants SEPARATION_CUTS=0 and zero hop-law violations.

Remaining defect is localised: exactly 4 nodes still carry two ports with the same parametric direction, and the motorcycle-diag counter shows exactly 4 'sharedFaceNodes' - crossings that nodeAtChartPoint merged into an existing face-interior node because their barycentric coordinates agree to within FaceChordWalk.MINIMUM_SEPARATION (1e-9). Two ruled-out explanations: nearCollinearSkips=0 (no same-axis chord pair is being rejected by the exact iso test at a gap below 1e-6) and foreignOriginSkips=0 (nothing is being skipped for landing on another trace's spawn point). So the last overlaps are two traces whose crossings with a third trace coincide to 1e-9 but which never produce a contact of their own.

Relaunch, fresh context. Reproduced the remaining defect exactly and named it. bolt at bias -1 (run-scene quad-layout --mesh bolt_in_tri.off --key 'K=curvature bias -1.0'): 151 of 154 cycles valid, hop-law violations 6, sharedFaceNodes 4, 4 nodes with ambiguous port order, and the lazy loop fires for 3 rounds. A segment dump of the two offending traces shows what the 4 shared nodes are: traces 0 and 2 are the two opposite separatrices of ONE cone (both spawn at chart point (24.5636,29.7025), axis V, signs +1 and -1) which, going round the closed surface, meet head-on on the same iso-line u=24.563628482974140 inside face 530. Trace 0 enters face 530 at v=-9.3068 with length 36.4243 going +v; trace 2 enters at v=-7.2183 with length 36.9208 going -v. The equal-time meeting point is v=-8.0143 at length 37.717. Instead each drove the WHOLE overlap and crashed at the far end: trace 0 ended at v=-7.979 (node 97, trace 2's entry) with ourLen=37.752, trace 2 ended at v=-9.3068 (node 101, trace 0's entry) with ourLen=39.009. Traces 27 and 28 are the same story at node 100 in face 3855.

Why the crash fires too late: a segment registers in FaceSegmentIndex only when its trace LEAVES the face, so two traces crossing one face concurrently are invisible to each other. earliestIntersection and the retroactive contactsOf sweep both only see laid chords, so the collinear crash the previous pass added can only fire after a full chord has been laid across the face - and the meetings recorded along that chord still become arcs, since buildTraceChains builds the chain from metOtherTraces regardless of where the trace died. That is exactly how the crossings with traces 7, 10 and 30 inside face 530 ended up noded twice (sharedFaceNodes=4) and how nodes 94, 97, 159 acquired two ports with the same parametric direction.

Fix, in the tracing: MotorcycleGraph now schedules a TYPE_HEAD_ON crash event. A trace's segment only enters FaceSegmentIndex when it leaves the face, so the graph additionally keeps tracesInFlightByFace - the traces that have entered each active face - and enqueueNextEvent asks headOnCrashDistance() for the nearest trace still crossing the same face on the same iso-line (exact iso equality, same axis, ahead of us). Per EGK*08 section 2 a motorcycle stops at the first point another reached no later: head-on that is the point where the two travelled lengths agree, distance = (theirLength + gap - ourLength)/2 (clamped to 0, skipped when it exceeds the gap because then the other's laid trail is the thing we will hit); same-direction a follower stops at the leader's entry point. handleHeadOnCrash lays BOTH traces' last chords up to that one point, nodes it once, records the meeting on both and ends both there, so no stretch of the shared iso-line ever carries two arcs and no crossing on it is noded twice.

bolt at curvatureBias -1 after the head-on fix, and this is the definition-of-done state: '[motorcycle] arrangement patches: 157 cycles, 157 valid rectangles, 0 unresolved', '[motorcycle] hop turns: flat=40 ccwCorner=0 cwCorner=588 atSingularity=40 lawViolations=0', '[motorcycle] Def 3.1 rectangularity: violations=0 worstRelativeError=0.000000', '[motorcycle] done traces=40 (covered=0) arcs=334 nodes=179 patches=157 retroactiveCrossings=6 collinearMeetings=2', '[quantize] arcs=334 classes=45 consistency=24 validity=40 (fallback=0) layout=69 prefixFallbacks=0', '[quantize] state=OPTIMAL objective=1903.657 zeroArcs=188/334 violations=0 round=0'. No separation round, no VALIDITY VIOLATION, no shared face nodes, no ambiguous port orderings. Against master at that bias: 289 cycles / 69 rectangles, 508 hop-law violations, 50 separation rounds and a merged cluster of six singularities.

And bolt at bias -1 now loads end to end for the first time: '[embed] arcs=334 copy V=4827 E=14475 F=9650 0.04s (carve 0.04 check 0.00)', the global grid relax converges (energy 3.48e+05 to 3.54e+04, flipped=0/7702), '[quad-extract] preimages ... quads=12021 euler=2', '[patch-grids] patches=42 directMatches=39 rejected=0'. Screenshot tmp/headon1-bolt.png shows the quad layout on the bolt. The two downstream failures this ticket flagged as out of scope (chord crossing copy edge 13373 held by arc 472 at -1; index -1 out of bounds at -0.5) were consequences of the broken arrangement and are gone.

Second half of the tracing fix, found by the bias sweep: the collinear test was exact and bolt at bias -0.5 needs a tolerance. With the head-on rule in but the iso comparison still bit-exact, -0.5 reported nearCollinearSkips=1361 (same-axis chord pairs whose spans overlap and whose iso values differ by less than a millionth) with worstIsoGap=2.27e-13 - pure rounding, because the two traces reach the face through different chains of chart transitions. So two traces on one line were invisible to each other and -0.5 kept 176 hop-law violations, 68 ambiguous port orderings and the full 50-round separation spin.
